correctness.rationale: An all-n iff proof reduces Jenča D1/D2 to union-of-block product rectangles and then to matching row/column color palettes. This forces exactly two stated forms and no others. Counting each unordered proper split gives 2^(s-1) choices, and group actions and coordinatewise congruences are classified separately. The standard-library checker exhaustively matches all set partitions and orbit partitions for n<=5, but the universal claim rests on the proof rather than finite data.

evidence: For an ordinary monoid, Jenča D2 says that each classwise set product must be a union of equivalence classes, with identity singleton.
For the rectangular band, block products have support exactly R(A) × C(B); coefficientwise semigroup Schur closure additionally requires multiplicity constancy.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The support criterion is equivalent to Jenča dimensionality but not equivalent to a semigroup congruence, automorphism orbit partition, or coefficientwise Schur ring. The explicit three-column unbalanced split satisfies all set-support conditions but has block-sum square coefficients 2 and 1 on different rows, so it fails the stronger Schur condition.

value.rationale: This is a complete and naturally motivated exact classification of finite lax monoid quotient relations, an algebraic notion newly formalized and distinguished from automorphism orbits. It gives a weighted-Stirling census, its generating function, the precise orbit and congruence subfamilies, and an explicit smallest within-family strict gap at a seven-element monoid. The unbalanced cases are not implied by the known Schur tables; the invariant has independent structural interpretation as a relational-monoid quotient.
